title: _at_ground reads all spot grades unfiltered, unlike _floating, so a main house on its own ground is judged 'raised' and dropped from the ground cut
detail: The docstring says the ground cut uses 'the ground _floating reads'. It doesn't. _floating (and so _meets_ground) first drops any spot grade at another building's walls ('A point at one of the `others`' walls ... is that building's ground, never these'), and only then fits the plane. _at_ground passes the raw `spots` straight to _ground_at. On a lot where outbuildings sit on lower ground with their own spot grades (a ridge-top house, with a shed in front and a garage behind, both 6 ft lower), the plane fitted over every point runs under the house. The house's own bottom (0) then looks higher than max(ground) (about -3.75), so the main house counts as 'raised off the ground'. Its whole area drops out of 'at the main grade level', a false overhang question appears, and every yard loses its 'to its walls at ground level' reading. Meanwhile _floating, with the filtered points, says this same house meets the ground. Reproduced: house box(10,40,35,60,0,30) with spot grades at its walls at 0; shed box(15,20,30,32,-6,4) and garage box(10,75,30,95,-6,4), each with spot grades at -6. Result: building_area value None, readings from above 1080 and at grade 580. 580 is just the shed and garage; the house's 500 sf is missing. The yards also lose the walls reading. At 7201d49 the same site read 1080/1080. _ground_at for the house's corners returns [-4.13, -3.75]; _floating([house], spots, [gar, shed]) returns None (meets). Not a false pass (the outcome is needs review), but the architect sees the house left out of its own ground area and a question that shouldn't be there.
evidence: _at_ground: `ground = _ground_at([p[:2] for f in building["faces"] for p in f["points"]], points) if points else None` / `rests = bottom <= (max(ground) if ground else plan_level) + TOL`; caller: `cut = ops.unary_union([_at_ground(b, plan_level, spots) for b in buildings])` with `spots = facts.get("grade_points")`; whereas _floating: `points = [p for p in points if not (theirs.distance(Point(p[:2])) <= SPOT_REACH and mine.distance(Point(p[:2])) > SPOT_REACH)]` before `ground = _ground_at(corners, points)`
pin: packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py: add a 'house on a ridge, outbuildings lower' row to test_every_known_shape_is_read_at_the_ground_as_it_should_be_all_at_once (house 0-30 at 0 with its spot grades, shed and garage at -6 with theirs). It asserts building_area (1080, 1080, no overhang question) and that the front yard keeps 'to its walls at ground level'. It fails on today's _at_ground (580 at grade).
suggested_fix: Pull _floating's 'points at another building's walls are that building's ground' filter into one helper (e.g. _own_points(buildings, points, others)). Use it in both _floating and _at_ground (pass the other buildings to _at_ground, as _meets_ground does), so the cut and the ground test read literally the same ground. When the filter leaves nothing, fall back to plan_level, never to 'raised'.

title: With no spot grades and an unknown or sloped ground, any solid above the lowest one is 'raised': the main house on higher ground drops out of the at-grade cut (round-6 behavior lost)
detail: With no spot grades, `rests` compares a solid's bottom with plan_level. When the ground isn't known (ground_is_flat None, or False / sloped_ground), plan_level = lo, the lowest bottom of ALL buildings. The comment just above it says the opposite: 'with no grade (not given, not known to be flat...) that is the building's own base, so the plan is still measured'. So a detached shed standing lower than the house makes the house itself 'raised'. Reproduced: house box(10,25,35,65,3,33), shed box(40,75,50,85,0,9), ground_is_flat False (or None), no spot grades. building_area value None, readings from above 1100 and at grade 100 (only the shed); front_yard loses 'to its walls at ground level'. At 7201d49 (round 6, the group rule: each unconnected solid cut at its own bottom) the same site read 1100/1100 with the walls reading kept. The round-7 rewrite threw away the group rule's answer for this case, and the 5-shape table has no unknown-ground or no-spot-grades multi-building row, so nothing caught it. No false pass, but a false overhang question and the main building missing from its own ground cut.
evidence: `rests = bottom <= (max(ground) if ground else plan_level) + TOL` with `plan_level = grade if (grade is not None and not why_grade) else lo` and `lo, hi = (min(zs), max(zs))` over every building; the comment at 1220-1223: 'with no grade ... that is the building's own base, so the plan is still measured'
pin: packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py: a table row 'house above a detached shed, ground not known (no spot grades, ground_is_flat None and False)' asserting building_area 1100/1100 with no overhang question, and front_yard keeping 'to its walls at ground level'. It fails on the current code (at grade 100).
suggested_fix: When no spot grades say where the ground is, decide 'rests' per connected group (_connected): a solid rests if its bottom is its own group's lowest bottom (a detached building stands on its own base, as the comment says). Only a solid raised above a connected neighbour's bottom (a balcony) is left out. With spot grades, keep the per-solid ground test (after the filtering fix). Then add both rows to the table so the per-shape table covers the no-spots path.

The defect is real in the PR's final code, which was rewritten specifically to decide per solid, but reviewers should know main already behaves this way.
